summary: SAML assertion containing duplicate Audience entries suppresses RBAC roles during console login
description:
Issue summary: Several internal users reported intermittent 403s when accessing the Redwood Console. Sessions were created, but RBAC roles were not applied, resulting in feature access missing (e.g., no access to Deployments view and Alerts).

Impact: A subset of employees (approx 12 people across eng and support) could log in to the Console but appeared to have no roles/permissions. This blocks investigation and on-call workflows for affected users. No customer-facing incidents reported.

Environment: prod | us-east. Affected clients use Okta SAML SSO via the internal Console SAML app.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Authenticate via Okta -> select Redwood Console app. 2) SAML response POST to /sso/callback. 3) Token created by sso-proxy successfully; user session established but /api/v1/me returns roles: [] and authorization checks fail with 403.

Observed behavior: sso-proxy logs show: "rbac: role extraction empty - assertion audience mismatch" and the downstream auth service returns a session with empty roles. Okta logs show a SAML assertion with two <Audience> elements (https://console.redwood.ai and https://session-api.redwood.ai).

Expected behavior: Assertion contains a single Audience targeted to the Console app; RBAC extractor should parse roles from attribute statements and apply cached group-to-role mappings.

Relevant logs/snippets: 
- sso-proxy: 2026-03-10T09:14:22Z WARN rbac.extractor: "audience mismatch: saw [https://session-api.redwood.ai https://console.redwood.ai] - rejecting role mapping"
- auth-service: 2026-03-10T09:14:22Z INFO session.create: "session created user=apatal roles=[] source=sso"
- Okta System Log (eventId=0oa1y9...): SAML Response issued contains two AudienceRestriction/Audience nodes for the Console app due to recent mapping change.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: Issue reported 2026-03-10 09:05 by on-call support. Initial triage by Support confirmed 403s with valid sessions. Identity team reproduced locally by crafting SAML assertions with duplicate Audience elements. Hypothesis: sso-proxy's SAML parser treats multiple Audiences as a non-console assertion, and the RBAC extractor bail-out logic returns empty roles when Audience list ordering doesn't match expected single value.

What we checked:
- Okta app mapping changes in last 48h: found change by Okta-admin (tgerstle) which added an Audience for session-api to the Console SAML app to support new CLI flow. That change caused assertions targeted at both console and session-api to be emitted.
- sso-proxy code path: assertion.AudienceRestriction.Audience[] was handled by a strict equality check against configured console_audience. If length >1, parser sets audience_ok=false and returns no roles.
- Auth service verified sessions with empty roles were created even though groups attribute was present. The RBAC extractor short-circuits early on audience check, so it never reads groups.

Partial reproduction steps used in test: generated SAML with Audiences ordered [session-api, console] and observed role suppression. Reordered to [console, session-api] and roles applied in some cases, indicating order sensitivity.

Related signals: no increase in 5xx or customer impact; monitoring alert on "session.roles.empty" triggered for internal accounts.
resolution_notes:
Immediate mitigation (2026-03-10 13:20): rolled back the Okta app audience change for the Console app (Okta-admin: tgerstle). This restored normal single-audience assertions and recovered roles for affected users.

Short-term fix applied (2026-03-11): updated sso-proxy to accept multiple Audience entries and match if any audience equals console_audience (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sso-proxy/pull/418). Deployed to prod in us-east canary and validated with affected users.

Longer-term actions:
- Add unit/integration tests for SAML assertions with multiple Audience elements and unordered lists.
- Add an assertion-lint step in CI that fails if Okta app mappings include audiences intended for unrelated apps.
- Create an Okta change control checklist item for adding Audience entries to existing apps.
- Add an alert in PagerDuty for >5 internal sessions created with roles=[] within 15m.

Status: mitigation complete, fix deployed to us-east. ID team owns follow-ups and runbook updates.
